parts.visual:
Startup A sells physical mattresses. For every $1,000 mattress they sell, it costs them $700 in factory labor and materials to make it. (30% Gross Margin). Startup B sells accounting software. For every $1,000 subscription they sell, it costs them $10 in AWS server space. (99% Gross Margin). Wall Street will value Startup B ten times higher than Startup A.

The Math of Scaling:
1. Gross Margin: The revenue left over *after* paying the direct costs of delivering the product (COGS). Software has high gross margins. Hardware and services have low gross margins.
2. Net Margin: The actual profit left over after paying for EVERYTHING (including marketing, office rent, and CEO salaries).
parts.audio: Not all revenue is created equal. A million dollars of software revenue is vastly more valuable than a million dollars of consulting revenue, because software margins mean almost all of that million dollars can be reinvested into growth.

questions.question: What does COGS stand for?
options: Cost of Goods Sold. It is the direct, unavoidable cost required to deliver one unit of your product. If you run a cloud software company, your COGS is basically just AWS server hosting and Stripe credit card fees.
questions.correct_answer: Cost of Goods Sold. It is the direct, unavoidable cost required to deliver one unit of your product. If you run a cloud software company, your COGS is basically just AWS server hosting and Stripe credit card fees.
questions.explanation: COGS is the baseline penalty for existing.

questions.question: Listen to the VC criticizing a 'tech' company. Why does the VC say it is actually a services company?
questions.tts_text: They claim to be an AI tech company. But every time they get a new client, they have to hire three human consultants to manually set up the system. Their Gross Margins are 40%. They are not a tech company; they are a consulting firm in disguise.
options: Services don't scale. True software companies have 80%+ gross margins because the code scales infinitely for free. If you have to hire humans to deliver the product, your margins collapse, and VCs will refuse to value you as a tech company.
questions.correct_answer: Services don't scale. True software companies have 80%+ gross margins because the code scales infinitely for free. If you have to hire humans to deliver the product, your margins collapse, and VCs will refuse to value you as a tech company.

questions.question: A startup has $1 Million in revenue, 85% Gross Margins, but is losing $500,000 a month (Negative Net Margin). Is this a broken company?
options: No, this is a classic healthy hyper-growth startup. The high Gross Margin proves the core product is wildly profitable. The Negative Net Margin just means they are intentionally spending all that profit (and VC cash) on marketing to grow faster.
Yes, the margins are too high.
questions.correct_answer: No, this is a classic healthy hyper-growth startup. The high Gross Margin proves the core product is wildly profitable. The Negative Net Margin just means they are intentionally spending all that profit (and VC cash) on marketing to grow faster.
questions.explanation: Negative net margin is a choice. Negative gross margin is a death sentence.

questions.question: Why did WeWork crash so spectacularly when it tried to go public?
options: They disguised low-margin real estate as high-margin tech. WeWork claimed to be a 'Tech Company', but their COGS (paying rent on massive office buildings) meant their Gross Margins were terrible. Wall Street realized they were just a landlord.
